name: virus-field-infection
title: Virus field & stochastic H→I infection

purpose.question:
Layered on the validated Increment-1 confluent sheet: does a diffusing,
decaying extracellular virus field (source-cited D/decay, target
diffusion length 5 cell diameters = 25 sites) and a stochastic,
virus-driven H -> I infection transition produce LOCAL lesion spread
(new infections cluster near existing infected cells, not uniformly
across the sheet) with population conserved?

report.title: Increment 2: virus field diffuses/decays and infection spreads locally — mechanism validated, reproduction still PENDING
report.objective: Drive the CPM engine's virus field (secretion from InfectedReleasing cells, diffusion, decay) together with a stochastic H -> I infection transition over the Increment-1 confluent 0.3mm/900-cell sheet for 60 updates (mcs_per_update=10), seeded with a small initial lesion (init_infected_frac=0.01, 9 of 900 cells), and measure whether the lesion grows and whether new infections stay local to existing infected cells (Task 2.3's integration test, `tests/test_influenza_virus_infection.py`).
report.conclusion: MECHANISM VALIDATED, REPRODUCTION NOT YET ATTEMPTED. Over 60 updates (0.3mm/900-cell sheet, init_infected_frac=0.01: 891 H + 9 I initial cells), n_I grew 9 -> 16 (7 new-infection events) with n_H shrinking 884 in lockstep (n_H + n_I conserved every update), and total_virus grew from 0.0 to 1216.34 (field sum) as the seeded I cells secreted. Locality is established with a DISCRIMINATING null-baseline test, not a loose absolute radius: the mean distance from each new infection to the nearest already-infected cell is ~0.61x (seed 17: actual_mean 15.0 vs a uniform-random null_mean 24.6 sites; ~0.58-0.67x observed across seeds/step counts) the mean nearest-infected distance a uniform-random still-susceptible cell would have had that same update — well under the 0.75x pass threshold. A shuffled-virus-field non-local sanity control of the same run instead gives ratio ~1.13 (at/above chance) and correctly FAILS that threshold, confirming the test rejects non-local spread rather than passing on any lesion shape. The first new infection appeared at update 21, 5.0 sites from the nearest already-infected cell, and the first 3 update-with-new-infections stayed under a tighter 50-site (2x diffusion-length) bound. With init_infected_frac=0.0 (no seed, no initial virus), n_I stayed 0 and no new infections occurred for the whole run (null control). This validates the MECHANISM (diffusing/ decaying field + locally-spreading stochastic infection) — it is NOT a claim that any of Sego et al. 2022's Figs 3B/5/7 quantitative targets are met; that evaluation is deferred to Increment 9 (the capstone).
report.main_insight: A population-conserving, spatially-local infection spread emerges from just two mechanisms (field diffusion + a per-cell stochastic H -> I draw driven by local field concentration) with no explicit "infect-my-neighbor" rule — new infections land ~0.6x as far from prior infection as a uniform-random null baseline (a discriminating test that a shuffled-field non-local control correctly fails at ~1.13x), because the field itself is spatially concentrated, not because the transition rule encodes locality directly.
report.caveat: This study has NO resistance/IFN gating (resist=0 throughout — the per-cell resistance state variable arrives in Increment 3), no death/recovery, and no immune cells (macrophages/NK/CD8+ T arrive in later increments). The virus secretion magnitude uses the documented z=1/per-pixel convention (`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/fields.py`'s `_virus_field_params`, pre-dim.z halving of the source's `secretion_g_vi` spread evenly over each cell's 25 pixels) — this reproduces the source's RATE convention but its exact magnitude against the paper's field scale is an Increment-9 calibration concern, not settled here. Locality is now established against a discriminating uniform-random null baseline (not just "within a loose radius") and a non-local shuffled-field control confirms the test has teeth, but the 7 new-infection events over 60 updates still come from ONE seed (17); this is a single-run demonstration of the mechanism's qualitative behavior (grows, is genuinely local relative to chance, conserves population), not a statistically characterized rate, and it is not a quantitative Fig-6 reproduction.

key_metrics.name: locality_null_ratio
key_metrics.value: ~0.61 (seed 17: actual_mean 15.0 / random_null_mean 24.6); ~0.58-0.67 across seeds/step counts, threshold <0.75

study_card.goal: Validate that the extracellular virus field diffuses/decays as specified and that a seeded lesion spreads locally via stochastic H -> I infection, with population conserved — no reproduction claim.
study_card.mechanism: A single diffusing/decaying "virus" field (source-cited D, decay, and per-pixel secretion rate from InfectedReleasing cells) drives a per-cell stochastic H -> I transition (Pr = 1 - exp(-g_hv * v_bar)) each update, layered on the Increment-1 confluent sheet.
study_card.why_before_next: Increment 3 (IFN + per-cell resistance) modulates THIS infection transition — the field and the base (resist=0) transition must be shown to behave sensibly (spread, stay local, conserve population) before adding a resistance gate on top of it.
study_card.expected_result: n_I grows from the seeded lesion over updates while n_H shrinks correspondingly (population conserved); new infections occur near already-infected cells (within a few multiples of the field's own diffusion length), not scattered uniformly across the sheet; with no seed, nothing happens.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is single-seed evidence (grows, is genuinely local vs a discriminating null baseline, conserves population) sufficient mechanism validation for Increment 2, deferring a systematic replicate sweep and quantitative figure match to the capstone?

question:
Does the extracellular virus field (source-cited diffusion coefficient and
decay rate, secreted by InfectedReleasing cells) diffuse and decay as
specified, and does a stochastic, field-driven H -> I infection transition
spread a seeded lesion LOCALLY (new infections cluster near existing
infected cells) rather than uniformly, with total cell population
conserved?
hypothesis:
Layered on the Increment-1 confluent sheet: a virus field secreted by a
small seeded lesion of InfectedReleasing (I) cells diffuses outward and
decays; a stochastic H -> I transition (rate = g_hv * local mean field
concentration) converts nearby Healthy (H) cells to Infected (I) over
time, with new infections landing close to already-infected cells (within
a few multiples of the field's own diffusion length) rather than
scattered across the whole sheet, and n_H + n_I conserved every update.
objective:
Wire the virus field (Task 2.1, `pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/fields.py`) and
the stochastic infection transition (Task 2.2,
`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/transitions.py`) together over the Increment-1
sheet, drive them for 60 updates from a small seeded lesion
(`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/run.py::run_virus_infection`, Task 2.3), and
report the measured spread/locality/null-control behavior from the
integration test (`tests/test_influenza_virus_infection.py`). Wrap the
same mechanism as a process-bigraph composite
(`pbg_cpm_studies.composites.influenza.viral_infection`, CPMProcess +
InfectionProcess wired through `fates`) for the dashboard live demo (Task
2.4, this study) — measurements come from `run_virus_infection`, not the
live-demo composite (see caveat and Task 2.3's report on why the two
paths use independent RNG streams and are not bit-identical).
description:
Increment 2 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder: adds ONE
diffusible field (virus) and ONE new cell-state transition (H -> I,
stochastic, field-driven) on top of the Increment-1 confluent epithelial
sheet. No resistance/IFN, no death/recovery, no immune cells — those
arrive in Increments 3+. The virus field's diffusion coefficient, decay
rate, and target diffusion length (5 cell diameters = 25 lattice sites)
are taken from the CC3D ViralInfectionVTM source (see
`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml`'s `virus:` block); the infection
rate coefficient `g_hv` is likewise source-cited. Two independent
seed-derived RNG streams make the driver run
(`run.run_virus_infection`) fully deterministic: one chooses the initial
lesion, a separate one drives the per-update stochastic transition.
claim:
The extracellular virus field diffuses and decays as specified, and a
seeded lesion of infected cells spreads via a stochastic, virus-driven
healthy-to-infected transition that stays local to existing infection,
with total cell population conserved throughout. This validates the
mechanism only — it is not a claim that any of Sego et al. 2022's
quantitative figure targets are met; that reproduction verdict remains
pending until the capstone increment.
expected_behavior: n_I grows from the seeded initial lesion over successive updates while n_H shrinks by the same amount each update (n_H + n_I conserved).
New infections occur close to already-infected cells (well under 3x the field's own 25-site diffusion length), not scattered uniformly across the sheet.
With no seeded lesion (init_infected_frac=0.0) and no initial virus, n_I stays 0 and no new infections occur for the whole run.

readouts.name: New-infection distance to nearest prior-infected cell, vs a uniform-random null baseline
readouts.description: For each of the 7 new-infection events over the 60-update run, Euclidean distance (lattice sites) from the newly-infected cell's centroid to the nearest already-infected cell's centroid: range 5.0-32.0 sites (raw), first new infection at update 21, distance 5.0 sites. The DISCRIMINATING readout compares this against a per-update uniform-random null baseline (mean nearest-prior-infected distance over the full still-susceptible cell population that update): actual_mean=15.0 sites vs random_null_mean=24.6 sites, ratio ~0.61 (seed 17; ~0.58-0.67 across seeds/step counts) — well under the 0.75x pass threshold. A shuffled-virus-field non-local sanity control of the same run gives ratio ~1.13 (at/above chance) and correctly fails that threshold, confirming the comparison discriminates real local spread from non-local placement rather than passing on any lesion shape.

Pass criterion: n_I grows and n_H shrinks correspondingly over 60

behavior_tests.name: New infections land closer to prior infection than random chance (locality)
behavior_tests.description:
Pass criterion (discriminating, not a loose absolute radius): the mean
new-infection distance-to-nearest-prior-infected-cell must be under
0.75x the mean nearest-prior-infected distance a uniform-random
still-susceptible cell would have had that same update (a per-update
population-mean null baseline). Measured: actual_mean=15.0 sites,
random_null_mean=24.6 sites, ratio ~0.61 (seed 17; ~0.58-0.67 across
seeds/step counts) — comfortably under 0.75. A shuffled-virus-field
non-local control of the same run gives ratio ~1.13 and correctly
FAILS this threshold, confirming the test has teeth (Task 2.3 fix
round 1, `tests/test_influenza_virus_infection.py::
test_new_infections_land_closer_to_prior_infection_than_random_chance`).
A secondary check also holds the first 3 updates with actual new
infections under a tighter 50-site (2x diffusion-length) absolute
bound.

findings.statement:
New infections land significantly closer to already-infected cells
than uniform-random placement would predict (~0.61x the chance
distance, discriminated against a per-update population-mean null
baseline, not a loose absolute radius) — spatial locality emerges from
the field's own diffusion length (25 sites) without any explicit
"infect-my-neighbor" rule in the transition itself, which only reads
local field concentration. A shuffled-field non-local control
correctly fails the same test (ratio ~1.13), confirming the locality
claim is genuinely earned rather than an artifact of a bound too loose
to discriminate.

conclusion:
MECHANISM VALIDATED, NOT REPRODUCED. The virus field diffuses/decays and
drives a population-conserving, spatially-local infection spread from a
seeded lesion (measured: n_I 9 -> 16, 7 new-infection events landing
~0.61x as far from a prior-infected cell as a uniform-random null
baseline would predict — a discriminating test a shuffled-field non-local
control correctly fails at ratio ~1.13; null control confirms no
spontaneous infection). This increment has
no resistance/IFN gating, no death/recovery, and no immune cells, and
makes NO claim about matching any of Sego et al. 2022's Figs 3B/5/7
quantitative acceptance bands — that reproduction verdict is PENDING until
Increment 9 (the capstone).

biological_summary:
A small seeded lesion of InfectedReleasing (I) epithelial cells secretes
virus into a diffusing, decaying extracellular field (source-cited
diffusion coefficient and decay rate; target diffusion length 5 cell
diameters = 25 lattice sites, per `pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml`
`virus:` block). Nearby Healthy (H) cells stochastically transition to
Infected as a function of the local mean field concentration they
experience (`Pr(infect) = 1 - exp(-g_hv * v_bar)`), so the lesion grows
outward from its seed rather than infecting uniformly at random across
the sheet. This reproduces the qualitative spatial-spread PHENOMENON that
underlies Sego et al. 2022's Fig 6 virus/infection spatial snapshots
(referenced qualitatively here — Fig 6 has no digitized acceptance band
in this workspace, unlike Figs 3B/5/7, which are cell-count time-series
targets, not spatial-pattern targets, and are therefore not the right
comparison for this study). There is no resistance/IFN response yet
(per-cell resistance stays 0 throughout — Increment 3 adds the type-I
IFN field and the resistance state variable that will begin to gate this
same transition), no cell death/recovery, and no immune cells.
key_assumptions: Virus secretion magnitude uses the documented z=1/per-pixel convention (`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/fields.py`'s `_virus_field_params` — the source's per-cell `secretion_g_vi` is halved to remove the source's z=2 slab thickness for our single-layer z=1 sheet, then spread evenly over each cell's 25 pixels). This reproduces the source's RATE convention faithfully but its exact absolute magnitude against the paper's published field scale is an Increment-9 calibration concern, not validated here.

resist=0 for every cell throughout this run — no IFN-driven resistance gating exists yet (Increment 3). The measured infection rate here is therefore an UPPER bound on what later increments will show once resistance suppresses some fraction of would-be infections.

Single seed (17) for both the initial-lesion choice and the stochastic transition (two independent streams, see `run.run_virus_infection` docstring) — the 7-event, ~0.61x-null-ratio locality result is a single-run demonstration (the ~0.58-0.67x range cited above spans a small number of seeds/step counts checked during test development, not a full replicate study), not a statistically characterized rate across a systematic replicate sweep.

The live-demo composite (`pbg_cpm_studies.composites.influenza.viral_infection`) and the measurement driver (`run.run_virus_infection`) use independent RNG streams for the same `seed` and are NOT expected to produce bit- identical trajectories (Task 2.3 report) — the composite exists for a fast dashboard demo, not as the source of this study's readouts.

literature_anchors.expectation: The virus field's diffusion length should be ~5 epithelial-cell diameters (source `exp_virus_dl` = exp_cell_diameter * 5.0).
literature_anchors.model_observable: pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/fields.py VIRUS_DIFFUSION_LENGTH_SITES = 25 sites (5 cell diameters x 5 sites/diameter); new-infection distances (5.0-32.0 sites, raw) land ~0.61x as far from prior infection as a uniform-random null baseline (ratio threshold <0.75; shuffled-field non-local control fails at ~1.13), and the first 3 updates with new infections stay under a tighter 50-site (2x diffusion-length) absolute bound.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Diffusion length wired into the field; the study's primary locality behavior test compares against a discriminating uniform-random null baseline (not a fixed multiple of this length), with the diffusion length itself used only for the secondary early-update absolute-bound check (50 sites = 2x). No acceptance-band comparison to a digitized figure yet.

literature_anchors.expectation: Sego et al. 2022 Fig 6 shows the spatial pattern of virus concentration and infected cells spreading outward from an initial lesion over simulated time.
literature_anchors.model_observable: This study's discriminating locality result (new infections land ~0.61x as far from prior infection as a uniform-random null baseline would predict, vs ~1.13x for a shuffled-field non-local control) is the same qualitative phenomenon (local outward spread from an active lesion) that Fig 6 depicts.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Referenced QUALITATIVELY only -- no digitized acceptance band exists for Fig 6 in this workspace (unlike Figs 3B/5/7, which are cell-count time-series targets in pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/targets/ and are not spatial-pattern targets). A quantitative Fig-6 comparison is not attempted by this study.

model_change.notes:
Wraps the existing CPMProcess (now with `n_fields=1`,
`secretory_types=[types.I]`, and a `fields:` spec entry from
`fields.virus_field_spec_entry()`) plus a new InfectionProcess wired
through the shared `fates` map (same down-scale-coupling convention as
`cpm.coupling`) -- the live-demo composite for the dashboard. The
readouts and behavior tests above are measured directly against
`run.run_virus_infection` (raw `cpm_core.World` loop, Task 2.3), not
through this process-bigraph composite; see key_assumptions for why the
two paths are not expected to be bit-identical.
